title: India's Exports Surge 15% in Q1 FY27 as FTA Network Pays Off
excerpt: Shipments to ASEAN and Africa led the growth, with engineering goods, gems, and electronics all posting double-digit gains as India pushes toward a $1 trillion export target.
body:
• India’s overall exports grew 15% year-on-year in Q1 FY27, with merchandise exports reaching $129.32 billion — a 15.92% increase
  • Exports to ASEAN surged 66.9% to $10.5 billion and to Africa by 53.1% to $9.6 billion, reflecting India’s FTA-driven diversification strategy
  • Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal expressed confidence in hitting the $1 trillion export target for FY27, up from $863 billion in FY26

India’s goods exports to free trade agreement partners posted strong growth in the first quarter of FY27 (April-June 2026), driven by a surge in shipments to ASEAN and African nations as recently concluded trade pacts began paying off, according to commerce ministry data.

Broad-Based Growth Across Regions

Overall exports rose 15% year-on-year in Q1 FY27, with merchandise exports climbing 15.92% to $129.32 billion. Total exports including services reached $232.73 billion, up 11.37%.

The most striking gains came from FTA partner regions. Exports to ASEAN jumped 66.9% to $10.5 billion from $6.3 billion a year earlier, while shipments to Africa surged 53.1% to $9.6 billion. Together, these two regions added over $7.6 billion in exports during April-May alone, according to Outlook Business.

Exports to South Asia rose 40.2% to $6.1 billion, North East Asia climbed 30.7% to $8.3 billion, and Oceania — covering Australia and New Zealand, both FTA partners — recorded a 29% increase to $2.1 billion. NAFTA remained India’s largest export destination at $19.3 billion, though growth there was a modest 2.6%.

Sector Leaders: Engineering and Gems

The growth was not driven by a single commodity. Engineering goods — covering machinery, auto components, and industrial equipment — rose 20.74%, a signal of real manufacturing strength. Gems and jewellery surged 34.64%, partly lifted by rising gold and silver prices. Organic and inorganic chemicals grew 19.42%, and electronics continued its double-digit expansion as India deepened its role in global electronics supply chains.

“Come out of the cosy comfort of the domestic market.”

— Piyush Goyal, Commerce and Industry Minister, at the Board of Trade meeting

The FTA Network Expands

India has signed nine free trade agreements in the past three-and-a-half years, covering 38 economies. Trade pacts with the UAE, Oman, Australia, the EFTA bloc, and Mauritius are already in force. The India-UK FTA came into effect on July 15, opening access to a market that imports nearly $900 billion worth of goods annually.

The landmark India-EU FTA, concluded in January 2026, will give preferential access across 97% of EU tariff lines, covering 99.5% of trade value. Labour-intensive sectors — textiles, leather, footwear, gems — currently facing EU duties of 10-26% will see full duty elimination.

The Commerce Ministry is also hiring 1,000 export facilitators to be deployed across states and districts, particularly to help smaller businesses navigate FTA opportunities.

Trade Deficit Remains a Concern

While export growth was strong, imports grew faster. The trade deficit widened to $37.42 billion in Q1 FY27, with June alone posting a $15.32 billion gap compared to $2.89 billion a year earlier. Analysts attribute the spike to temporary restocking after oil supply disruptions and elevated precious metals imports rather than a structural shift, but the next few months of data will be critical.

The Road to $1 Trillion

India’s total exports hit a record $863 billion in FY26, including $442 billion in merchandise and $421 billion in services. Commerce Minister Goyal has set a $1 trillion target for FY27, which would require 17% merchandise export growth and 11% services growth.

Negotiations continue with the GCC, Canada, Israel, Chile, and the Maldives. The strategy of diversifying beyond North America and Europe appears to be working: regions outside these traditional markets now account for more than half of India’s exports.
